criteria.reason: The trade notice directs identification, isolation, stop sale/use, disposition, sanitation, onward notification, acknowledgement, findings, and close-out evidence without claiming completion.

evidence.quote: Please use the attached register to check for affected stock. Stop sale and use of matching products, isolate them, and carry out the disposal or destruction requested in the notices. Clean and sanitize surfaces and containers that contacted the products. Hold unidentified or partly labelled stock separately while Purchasing obtains photographs, purchase records and supplier confirmation.

If you supplied affected products onward, promptly pass the identification and action instructions to those customers, using your delivery records. Ask them to confirm receipt and report their findings. Return your response to the contact that sent you this notice, including an explicit nil holding where checked; do not wait for a positive stock finding before acknowledging receipt.

Customers holding affected products were asked to stop eating them, discard or destroy them, and clean and
sanitize surfaces and containers that had contacted them. Products were expected to be off retail shelves at the
time of the notice, but could remain in home refrigerators or freezers.

criteria.reason: The notice presents N02 as four supplemental packs, preserves the earlier scope and dates, distinguishes sale and package-date bases, and does not misstate the first retailer-notification date.

evidence.quote: N02 adds four packs to N01: Bunny Luv 50 lb; Cal-Organic 15 lb and 50 lb; and Good & Gather 1 lb. The other N01 products remain in scope. The 2pk/2lbs description has not been interpreted as two separate 2 lb bags. Downstream date windows are kept separately from the upstream retail sale period.

N02 records additions to the public notice, not the first date on which those retailers were notified: its account says retailers received all correct pack-size details on November 16. Do not treat November 21 as permission to release earlier matching stock.

This notice expands the whole-carrot packs covered by the November 16 recall. The table lists the pack
combinations for the brands concerned. The original retail sale period, August 14 through October 23, 2024, and
the other recalled products remain applicable. These packs have no Best-if-Used-by date.

The company reported that retailers receiving affected products had been notified of all correct pack sizes when the
recall began on November 16. This notice updates the published pack list; it does not establish the first date of
retailer notification.

criteria.reason: It distinguishes products from customer relationships, treats state lists as overall distribution requiring transaction evidence, and preserves the broader original Grimmway geography.

evidence.quote: The two downstream notices give 11 product/channel relationships. A state list describes overall distribution; individual product deliveries require transaction evidence. Wild Harvest is one product with two channel relationships, rather than two distinct products.

Grimmway | N01 describes distribution nationwide in the United States, Puerto Rico and Canada, including supply links to F&S and 4Earth. | The downstream state lists do not restrict the original carrot recall. Check actual customer deliveries; obtain lot and processing records.

File contents: notices and the product/customer lists above. Inventory balances, production lots, receiving and
dispatch transactions, disposition quantities and customer acknowledgements were not attached. Reference
numbers are file identifiers, not production lot numbers.

Grimmway Farms recalled the organic whole carrots and peeled baby carrots listed below because they may be
contaminated with Shiga toxin-producing E. coli O121:H19. The products were shipped directly to retail distribution
centers nationwide in the United States, Puerto Rico and Canada.

criteria.reason: The four-notice historical cutoff is explicit, actions remain open, and expiry, expected shelf absence, illness reports, and frozen-stock status are not treated as clearance.

evidence.quote: For the notice log, N02 is dated November 21 and was published November 22; N04 is dated November 26 and was published December 2. The review covers N01–N04 at this historical cutoff. Later notices require a separate update.

The attached notices do not include those counts or completion records. Actions remain open. Expiry, an expectation that stock is no longer on sale, or an absence of reported illness does not establish clearance; frozen holdings still need checking under the recall identification rules.

4Earth had not received reports of related illness when it issued the notice. The products were more than three
weeks past their dates, but could remain in home refrigerators or freezers. Customers were asked to stop eating or
using them, discard them, and clean and sanitize contact surfaces.
